**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 18](https://www.sefaria.org/Pri_Etz_Chaim,_Gate_of_the_Sabbath.18)** (Kabbalah) — The Arizal's teaching on the three Shabbat meals calls the third meal "an inheritance without boundaries," because at that hour no kelipah holds sway and Ze'ir Anpin rises close to the "supernal brow" of Atika; this meal is tied to the verse "and I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father." Rav Tzadok builds on the same pairing of the third meal, the boundless inheritance and the revelation of Atika.
וְזֶהוּ נִקְרָא נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים, כִּי אֵין קְלִיפָּה שׁוֹלֶטֶת שָׁם
sefaria: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 18

notes.text: **[Isaiah 58:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Isaiah.58.14)** — אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה' וְהִרְכַּבְתִּיךָ עַל בָּמֳתֵי אָרֶץ וְהַאֲכַלְתִּיךָ נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִיךָ — "Then you shall delight in Hashem, and I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth, and feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father." The same verse supplies "Then you shall delight in Hashem" (3.30), which the Tanchuma reads as the merit of Shabbat. *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar II 88b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Yitro.27.457)** (Yitro) — בִּסְעוּדָתָא תְּלִיתָאָה דְּשַׁבְּתָא, כְּתִיב וְהַאֲכַלְתִּיךָ נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִיךָ. דָּא הִיא סְעוּדָתָא דִּזְעֵיר אַפִּין, דְּהַוֵי בִּשְׁלֵימוּתָא — "Of the third meal of Shabbat it is written, 'and I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father': this is the meal of Ze'ir Anpin, which is in completeness." Rav Tzadok opens with these words verbatim. On the same daf ([Zohar, Yitro 27:454](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Yitro.27.454)) R. Shimon, on completing the third meal, would have the whole verse proclaimed over him. *Mafteach: found*

**[Shabbat 118a–b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.118a)** — כָּל הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נוֹתְנִין לוֹ נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים ... לֹא כְּאַבְרָהָם ... וְלֹא כְּיִצְחָק ... אֶלָּא כְּיַעֲקֹב, שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ "וּפָרַצְתָּ יָמָּה וָקֵדְמָה וְצָפוֹנָה וָנֶגְבָּה" — "Whoever delights in Shabbat is given an inheritance without boundaries ... not like Avraham ... nor like Yitzchak ... but like Yaakov, of whom it is written, 'and you shall spread out westward and eastward, northward and southward.'" The statement of R. Yochanan begins at the foot of [118a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.118a) and ends at the top of [118b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.118b); Rav Tzadok's "בלא מצרים" is the reading of Ein Yaakov, where the Vilna text has "בלי מצרים". *Mafteach: found*

**[Genesis 28:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.28.14)** — וְהָיָה זַרְעֲךָ כַּעֲפַר הָאָרֶץ וּפָרַצְתָּ יָמָּה וָקֵדְמָה וְצָפֹנָה וָנֶגְבָּה — "Your offspring shall be like the dust of the earth, and you shall spread out westward and eastward, northward and southward." God's promise at Beit El as Yaakov leaves for Charan; Rav Tzadok returns to it in 4.32, reading it as the holiness of the Land going with him wherever he goes. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 11:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.11.7)** — אַבְרָהָם שֶׁאֵין כָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת, יָרַשׁ אֶת הָעוֹלָם בְּמִדָּה ... אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיִּחַן אֶת פְּנֵי הָעִיר, נִכְנַס עִם דִּמְדּוּמֵי חַמָּה, וְקָבַע תְּחוּמִין מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם, יָרַשׁ אֶת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹא בְּמִדָּה — "Avraham, of whom Shabbat-keeping is not written, inherited the world in measure ... but Yaakov, of whom it is written ('he encamped before the city,' Gen. 33:18: he arrived at dusk and set Shabbat boundaries while it was still day), inherited the world without measure." From this Midrash Rav Tzadok draws that the boundless inheritance is earned through Shabbat itself. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Vayishlach 1](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Vayishlach_1) (Rav Tzadok) — cites the same Bereshit Rabbah 11 and "ופרצת ימה" as a "נחלה בלא מצרים" promised to Yaakov when he left his father, and adds that it rests on "ושמרתיך בכל אשר תלך": being guarded from all evil is what lets Yaakov and his seed overcome every nation. *checked*
[Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayetzei 1](#/read/Beit_Yaakov_on_Torah,_Vayetzei_1) (Ishbitz–Radzin) — opens Parshas Vayetzei, as this os does, by joining "ויצא יעקב ... ופרצת ימה" to "אם תשיב משבת רגלך ... והאכלתיך נחלת יעקב אביך", and reads Shabbat delight as cleaving to what is "high above the high"; it also calls whoever accepts the yoke of Heaven "the greatest free man," which matches Rav Tzadok's closing on the yoke of Torah. *checked*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 68:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.68.13)** — רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי פָּתַר קְרָיָה בַּגָּלוּת, וַיֵּצֵא יַעֲקֹב מִבְּאֵר שָׁבַע, הֵאיךְ מָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר: שַׁלַּח מֵעַל פָּנַי וְיֵצֵאוּ — "R. Yehoshua ben Levi read the passage as speaking of exile: 'And Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva' — as it says, 'Send them away from My presence and let them go out.'" The Midrash goes on to read every clause of the passage (Charan, the place, the stones, the ladder) as the destruction and the Babylonian exile. It is the second-to-last siman of parashah 68 in Sefaria's numbering. *Mafteach: found*

**[Jeremiah 15:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jeremiah.15.1)** — אִם יַעֲמֹד מֹשֶׁה וּשְׁמוּאֵל לְפָנַי אֵין נַפְשִׁי אֶל הָעָם הַזֶּה שַׁלַּח מֵעַל פָּנַי וְיֵצֵאוּ — "Even if Moshe and Shmuel stood before Me, My heart would not turn to this people: send them away from My presence and let them go out." The verse of the exile that the Midrash sets against "ויצא יעקב". *Mafteach: missing*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 75:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.75.8)** — וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁבֵּרְכוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָבִיו לָמָּה חָזַר וּבֵרְכוֹ ... אֶלָּא שֶׁרָאָה יִצְחָק בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁעֲתִידִין בָּנָיו לְהִגָּלוֹת לְבֵין הָאֻמּוֹת, אָמַר לוֹ בּוֹא וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ בְּרָכוֹת שֶׁל גָּלֻיּוֹת שֶׁיַּחְזֹר עָלֶיךָ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וִיקַבֶּצְךָ מִבֵּין הַגָּלֻיּוֹת — "Since God had blessed him, why did his father bless him again (Gen. 28:1)? Yitzchak saw that his sons would be exiled among the nations, and said: Come, I will bless you with blessings for exiles, that God will return and gather you from among the exiles." The second blessing was given as Yaakov set out for Charan, so the departure itself is marked as the beginning of exile. *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar I 148b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei.7.41)** (Vayetzei) — וַיֵּצֵא יַעֲקֹב מִבְּאֵר שָׁבַע וַיֵּלֶךְ חָרָנָה, רָמַז כַּד נָפְקוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִבֵּי מַקְדְּשָׁא, וְאִתְגָּלוּ בֵּינֵי עַמְמַיָא, כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמֵר וַיֵּצֵא מִן בַּת צִיּוֹן כָּל הֲדָרָהּ — "'And Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva and went to Charan' alludes to when Israel went out of the Temple and were exiled among the nations, as it says, 'And there went out from the daughter of Zion all her splendor.'" *Mafteach: found*

**[Lamentations 1:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Lamentations.1.6)** — וַיֵּצֵא מִן בַּת צִיּוֹן כָּל הֲדָרָהּ — "And there went out from the daughter of Zion all her splendor." The ketiv is מן בת and the qere מִבַּת; Rav Tzadok, like the Zohar, writes the ketiv. *Mafteach: found*

**[Ramban on Genesis 12:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Ramban_on_Genesis.12.6)** — אוֹמַר לְךָ כְּלָל תָּבִין אוֹתוֹ בְּכָל הַפָּרָשִׁיּוֹת הַבָּאוֹת בְּעִנְיַן אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב ... כָּל מָה שֶׁאֵרַע לָאָבוֹת סִימָן לַבָּנִים. וְלָכֵן יַאֲרִיכוּ הַכְּתוּבִים בְּסִפּוּר הַמַּסָּעוֹת ... וְכֻלָּם בָּאִים לְלַמֵּד עַל הֶעָתִיד — "I will give you a rule for all the coming passages about Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov ... whatever happened to the fathers is a sign for the children; therefore Scripture dwells on the journeys ... all of it comes to teach about the future." This is the Ramban's programmatic statement of the principle; he applies it to the patriarchs' journeys throughout his commentary. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Deuteronomy 28:48](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.28.48)** — וְעָבַדְתָּ אֶת אֹיְבֶיךָ ... בְּרָעָב וּבְצָמָא וּבְעֵירֹם וּבְחֹסֶר כֹּל — "You shall serve your enemies ... in hunger and in thirst, in nakedness and in want of everything." Rav Tzadok describes Yaakov's flight in the words of the Tochachah's exile, unnamed. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Genesis 32:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.32.11)** — קָטֹנְתִּי מִכֹּל הַחֲסָדִים וּמִכָּל הָאֱמֶת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתָ אֶת עַבְדֶּךָ כִּי בְמַקְלִי עָבַרְתִּי אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן הַזֶּה וְעַתָּה הָיִיתִי לִשְׁנֵי מַחֲנוֹת — "I am too small for all the kindnesses ... for with my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps." Yaakov left with nothing but his staff. *Mafteach: found*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 68:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.68.2)** — רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָן פָּתַח: שִׁיר לַמַּעֲלוֹת אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי אֶל הֶהָרִים, אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי אֶל הַהוֹרִים לְמַלְפָנַי וְלִמְעַבְּדָנַי. מֵאַיִן יָבוֹא עֶזְרִי ... וַאֲנִי לֹא נֶזֶם אֶחָד וְלֹא צָמִיד אֶחָד — "'I lift my eyes to the mountains' — to my parents, my teachers and those who conceived me. 'From where will my help come?' Eliezer went with ten camels ... and I have not one ring, not one bracelet." The petichta to the parashah puts Psalm 121 in Yaakov's mouth as he leaves empty-handed. *Mafteach: found*
In the print the words "וכמ"ש" (3 words on, at 2.41) stand with nothing quoted after them. The Midrash as opened here does not speak of the exile of Jerusalem, so "as is written" most likely points back to the exile readings just cited (Bereshit Rabbah 68:13 and Zohar I 148b), or a word such as "שם" has dropped out.

**[Psalms 121:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms.121.1)** — שִׁיר לַמַּעֲלוֹת אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי אֶל הֶהָרִים מֵאַיִן יָבֹא עֶזְרִי — "A song of ascents: I lift my eyes to the mountains; from where will my help come?" *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Vayetzei 2](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Vayetzei_2) (Rav Tzadok) — the passage "explained above": it opens with the same petichta of Bereshit Rabbah 68 ("אשא עיני אל ההרים ... מאין יבא עזרי") and reads Yaakov's fear on going to Charan as fear of Esav and Lavan's influence, from which only Torah and attachment to Hashem protect him. *checked*

**[Pesach Haggadah, Magid, First Fruits Declaration 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesach_Haggadah,_Magid,_First_Fruits_Declaration.2)** — צֵא וּלְמַד מַה בִּקֵּשׁ לָבָן הָאֲרַמִּי לַעֲשׂוֹת לְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ: שֶׁפַּרְעֹה לֹא גָזַר אֶלָּא עַל הַזְּכָרִים, וְלָבָן בִּקֵּשׁ לַעֲקֹר אֶת הַכֹּל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: אֲרַמִּי אֹבֵד אָבִי — "Go out and learn what Lavan the Aramean sought to do to Yaakov our father: Pharaoh decreed only against the males, but Lavan sought to uproot everything, as it says, 'An Aramean [sought to] destroy my father.'" *Mafteach: missing*
sefaria: Pesach Haggadah, Magid, First Fruits Declaration 2

notes.text: **[Pesach Haggadah, Magid, In the Beginning Our Fathers Were Idol Worshipers 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesach_Haggadah,_Magid,_In_the_Beginning_Our_Fathers_Were_Idol_Worshipers.5)** — וְהִיא שֶׁעָמְדָה לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ וְלָנוּ ... שֶׁבְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר עוֹמְדִים עָלֵינוּ לְכַלוֹתֵנוּ, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַצִּילֵנוּ מִיָּדָם — "And it is this that has stood by our fathers and us ... for in every generation they rise against us to destroy us, and the Holy One, blessed be He, saves us from their hand." Rav Tzadok reads "צא ולמד" as the proof of this paragraph: Lavan is the first instance of "in every generation." *Mafteach: missing*
sefaria: Pesach Haggadah, Magid, In the Beginning Our Fathers Were Idol Worshipers 5

notes.text:
**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Sefat Emet, Genesis, Bereshit 13](https://www.sefaria.org/Sefat_Emet,_Genesis,_Bereshit.13)** (Chassidus) — The Torah opens "בראשית" for the sake of Israel, who are called "reishit," the first-fruit portion of creation that raises the rest of the world to its root; the same piece goes on to the Shabbat delight that earns "a boundless inheritance, the inheritance of Yaakov." It joins reishit, Israel's root in creation, and Shabbat as Rav Tzadok does.
וזה ענין הראשית שהיא העיקר והתכלית

**[Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tavo 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma,_Ki_Tavo.1)** — בּוֹא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה מִתְחַטְּאִין, וְכַמָּה יֵשׁ לָהֶן פִּתְחוֹן פֶּה לְעוֹשֵׂי מִצְוֹת ... מַנִּיחוֹ בַּסַּל וְהוֹלֵךְ לִירוּשָׁלַיִם ... וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר, אֵינִי זָז מִכָּאן עַד שֶׁתַּעֲשֶׂה צָרְכִּי הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה — "Come and see how fondly those who do mitzvos plead, how much they may say ... he places [the first fruits] in a basket, goes to Jerusalem ... and moreover he would say: I will not move from here until You fulfill the needs of this day." The same Midrash supports reading צרכי at 3.61 as "the needs of [this day]". *Mafteach: missing*

**[Midrash Tanchuma, Re'eh 11](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma,_Re'eh.11)** — בִּזְכוּת שְׁנֵי דְּבָרִים, יִשְׂרָאֵל מִתְחַטְּאִין לִפְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם, בִּזְכוּת שַׁבָּת, וּבִזְכוּת מַעַשְׂרוֹת. בִּזְכוּת שַׁבָּת, דִּכְתִיב: אִם תָּשִׁיב מִשַּׁבָּת רַגְלֶיךָ. מַה כְּתִיב בַּתְרֵיהּ, אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה' — "In the merit of two things Israel plead fondly before the Omnipresent: the merit of Shabbat and the merit of tithes. Of Shabbat it is written, 'If you restrain your foot because of Shabbat'; and after it, 'Then you shall delight in Hashem.'" Rav Tzadok cites only the Shabbat half; the second merit, tithes, is the declaration that follows bikkurim in Devarim 26. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Shabbat 118b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.118b)** — אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נוֹתְנִין לוֹ מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהִתְעַנַּג עַל ה' וְיִתֶּן לְךָ מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבֶּךָ". עוֹנֶג זֶה אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מַהוּ. כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר "וְקָרָאתָ לַשַּׁבָּת עוֹנֶג" — הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר זֶה עוֹנֶג שַׁבָּת — "Whoever delights in Shabbat is given the requests of his heart ... I do not know what this delight is; when it says 'and you shall call Shabbat a delight', say: this is the delight of Shabbat." "There" refers to the same sugya (Shabbat 118) he cited in 1.4. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Sefat Emet, Genesis, Vayetzei 20](https://www.sefaria.org/Sefat_Emet,_Genesis,_Vayetzei.20)** (Chassidus) — "And Yaakov went out" is both the exile after the Temple and every Motza'ei Shabbat. Yaakov "helps us in exile," so wherever Israel struggle to find a point of holiness he is with them, and the Shabbat delight that earns "a boundless inheritance ... ופרצת ימה" is the holiness of Shabbat staying with a person into the weekdays. This is close to Rav Tzadok's reading of the third meal as holiness that goes with a person wherever he goes.
לכן בכל מקום שבנ"י בגלות מייגעין עצמן למצוא נקודה קדושה. יעקב אע"ה מסייע לנו

**[Psalms 27:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms.27.4)** — אַחַת שָׁאַלְתִּי מֵאֵת ה' אוֹתָהּ אֲבַקֵּשׁ שִׁבְתִּי בְּבֵית ה' כָּל יְמֵי חַיַּי לַחֲזוֹת בְּנֹעַם ה' וּלְבַקֵּר בְּהֵיכָלוֹ — "One thing I asked of Hashem, that I seek: that I may dwell in the house of Hashem all the days of my life." Read here as the house of Hashem that goes with a person wherever he is. *Mafteach: found*

**[Isaiah 14:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Isaiah.14.3)** — וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם הָנִיחַ ה' לְךָ מֵעָצְבְּךָ וּמֵרָגְזֶךָ וּמִן הָעֲבֹדָה הַקָּשָׁה אֲשֶׁר עֻבַּד בָּךְ — "On the day Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, your trembling, and the hard labor with which you were made to serve." The Masoretic text spells עֻבַּד defectively; the print has עובד. *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar I 48a–b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Bereshit.78.196)** (Bereshit) — וְדָא תּוֹסֶפֶת יַהֲבַת לְעַלְמָּא קַדִּישָׁא. וּבְהַהוּא תּוֹסֶפֶת חָדָאן וְיִתְנְשֵׁי מִנַּיְיהוּ כָּל מִלִּין דְּחוֹל וְכָל צַעֲרִין וְכָל עָאקִין כְּמָא דְאַתְּ אָמֵר בְּיוֹם הָנִיחַ יְיָ לְךָ מֵעָצְבְּךָ וּמֵרָגְזֶךָ וּמִן הָעֲבֹדָה הַקָּשָׁה — "This addition [of soul] she gives to the holy people; with it they rejoice and forget all weekday matters, all sorrows and troubles, as it says, 'on the day Hashem gives you rest ...'" The paragraph runs from the end of 48a onto 48b; the words Rav Tzadok relies on stand right after the start of 48b, as he says (רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב). *Mafteach: found*

connector.why: Same image of Israel in Egypt as a fetus enclosed by Egypt's impurity (גוי מקרב גוי) and exile as preparation for Torah through suffering (Berachot 5a, 600,000 souls).
Same Bereshit Rabbah 11 and Shabbat 118 nachala bli metzarim promised to Yaakov when he left, tied to ושמרתיך בכל אשר תלך.
Same Tanchuma Ki Tavo / Re'eh 11 / Shabbat 118b chain on mitchat'in, bikkurim and Shabbat granting the heart's requests.
Shares Zohar I 148b and Lam 1:6 by citation only; its theme is Yaakov as Adam before the sin, not exile.
Ishbitz–Radzin list: opens Vayetzei with ופרצת ימה and Isaiah 58 (Shabbat delight, nachalat Yaakov); develops Shabbat delight and freedom through the yoke of Heaven.

found.ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 18
found.why: Third meal = nachala bli metzarim with no kelipah, tied to והאכלתיך נחלת יעקב and the revelation of Atika.
Yaakov's going out as exile and Motza'ei Shabbat; Shabbat's boundless inheritance as holiness accompanying Israel into exile.
Maharal on why the Haggadah opens with Lavan who sought to uproot all: causeless enmity recurring in every generation.
Israel as reishit for whom Bereishit was written, joined with Shabbat delight and nachalat Yaakov.
